name: Network hotfixes
note: Advisory rows are the vendor or NVD link CISA published for each threat in data/threats.json. The checklist rows are short notes from public guides fetched with this list. This is defensive guidance for your own network.

entries.title: Patch Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS
entries.fix: Install the current security update for Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS. If the vendor has no fix, take that product off the internet.
entries.cisaAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

checklist.title: Install software and firmware updates
checklist.detail: Software and app updates contain security fixes that protect devices. On a router, firewall, VPN, or NAS, install the vendor firmware update the same way.

checklist.title: Turn on 2-step verification
checklist.detail: NCSC recommends 2-step verification to protect online accounts. Use it on email, the router admin page, and anywhere a password is the only lock.

checklist.title: Use a strong, separate password for email
checklist.detail: NCSC says a criminal who gets your email can reach many other accounts. Use a password manager, and make the email password strong and different from the rest.

checklist.title: Back up the files you cannot replace
checklist.detail: NCSC says to safeguard important data by backing it up to an external drive or cloud storage.

checklist.title: Turn on authentication and encryption on the router
checklist.detail: The CIS telework and small-office guide recommends enabling authentication and encryption on home routers and modems, which are the on-ramp from your network to the internet.

checklist.title: Turn off router services you do not use
checklist.detail: The same CIS guide says to turn off unneeded services that an attacker can use, and to maintain the device and dispose of it with care when you replace it.

checklist.title: Read the small-office network guides NIST points to
checklist.detail: NIST Small Business Cybersecurity Corner lists a firewall overview, the NSA home-network best practices, and the CIS telework guide for securing routers and modems.
